extraction.name: TravelPlanner
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating language agents on real-world travel planning with tool use and multiple constraints, providing a sandbox environment, tools over nearly four million records, and 1,225 curated queries with reference plans.
extraction.creator: Jian Xie; Kai Zhang; Jiangjie Chen; Tinghui Zhu; Renze Lou; Yuandong Tian; Yanghua Xiao; Yu Su
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was constructed by creating a static closed sandbox environment, designing diverse travel queries from sampled trip elements and constraints, generating natural-language queries with GPT-4, and obtaining human-annotated reference plans followed by author review and budget recalibration.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data came from publicly available Internet sources, including Kaggle datasets for flights, restaurants, and accommodations, plus Google Distance Matrix API and Google Places API results, which were stored in static databases.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The collected source data were modified by adding, deleting, and altering keys and values; prices and categorical attributes were also generated or randomly assigned for some resources to fit benchmark requirements.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The environment was standardized into a static database; selected fields were extracted from source datasets, other values discarded, API results stored for consistency, and query budgets recalibrated using annotated plan costs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Twenty graduate students manually annotated plans for synthesized queries. A plan was accepted only if it satisfied all constraints in the evaluation script. Authors then reviewed every query-plan pair and corrected errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotated plans underwent multiple stages of human verification, detailed author review, and validation to ensure each query had at least one feasible solution.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 for natural language query generation; GPT-4-Turbo for extracting key plan components into structured form
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state they will release evaluation scripts, but no update schedule or deprecation policy is specified.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Travel preferences and constraints such as budget, room rules, room type, cuisine preferences, transportation preferences, number of people, and whether travelers have pets or children under 10.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to support future research on complex planning and may help automate tedious planning tasks, but the authors note that commonsense definitions may vary and encourage broader discussion; they also prohibit cheating on validation and test sets.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential bias may arise from using authors' consensus to define commonsense constraints and from source data derived from publicly available Internet content.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark uses a static closed sandbox rather than dynamic real-world data, commonsense criteria are based on authors' consensus, and current agents perform poorly especially under multiple constraints and long-horizon planning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating language agents for tool use and complex multi-constraint planning; includes training, validation, and test splits, with evaluation feedback encouraged for training but no cheating allowed on validation and test sets.
